markdown_report:
### Insights

**Starting point.** (1) SASRec models ordered context; an independent recent-history branch tests whether older interactions dilute current intent. Recency does not establish ownership or satisfied demand. (2) Electronics has 14.95% sampled wrong rankings and a −0.4812 lower-decile margin, motivating stronger candidate competition without establishing HR@10 gains. (3) Embedding similarities of 0.5392–0.5566 provide little evidence of severe collapse, making diversification a lower priority.

**Related work.** (1) [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) motivates calibrated multiple-negative BCE; its calibration depends on sampling assumptions. (2) [HeteroTempRec](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ins.2025.122703) motivates temporal fusion, but does not validate this adaptation. (3) [DTR4Rec](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10489-024-05875-3) motivates directional continuation, which cannot establish compatibility or satisfied demand.

### Framework and candidate ideas

Cross **context selection**—full history, recent history, directed transitions—with **candidate discrimination**—single-negative BCE or multiple-negative calibrated BCE. This separates stale-context errors from weak margins.

Scores are Originality / Potential / User alignment / Model alignment / Difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Benefits and limitations apply respectively to those dimensions.

| Idea | Scores | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Multiple-negative gBCE | 3/7/4/9/3 | + Established combination, reusable objective, candidate specificity, direct margin target, compact loss; − incremental, uncertain transfer, no temporal correction, sampled-margin proxy, sampler subtleties. |
| Recent-window gate | 4/7/8/5/5 | + Compact adaptation, reusable temporal pathway, targets stale interests, potentially separates confusing contexts, shared weights; − familiar, may discard enduring preferences, no compatibility proof, indirect margin effect, independent windows required. |
| Directed-transition residual | 5/7/7/6/5 | + Distinct continuation evidence, reusable graph, targets unsupported adjacency, extra ranking signal, sparse implementation; − established precedent, sparse edges, no compatibility guarantee, popularity shortcuts, extra serving state. |
| **Recent-window gate with gBCE** | **4/8/8/9/6** | + Complementary mechanisms, extensible framework, targets two user failures, targets weak separation, modular components; − modest novelty, uncertain interaction, no satisfaction labels, unproven HR transfer, greater compute and ablation cost. |

### Selected proposal

At 0% progress, retain **recent-window gated SASRec with multiple-negative gBCE**, implementing gBCE first and independently ablating both components. It targets **older or isolated interactions treated as current demand**, **broad historical associations displacing recent specific interests**, and measured weak separation.

Independently encode raw five-item windows using shared weights and branch-local positions; stacked local attention does not enforce this horizon ([Longformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.05150)). Mix recent and full features using a small gate. Use 128 uniform negatives and the exact published calibrated loss; sampling exclusions invalidate its original calibration assumptions.

Preserve four routes, seeds, splits, evaluator, predictor serialization, and diagnostic interfaces. Compare baseline, gate-only, gBCE-only, and combined variants under the shared GPU budget. Predeclare checkpoint selection and report category regressions; paired within-category bootstrap intervals remain exploratory after selection. Sampled HR@10 does not establish full-catalog superiority ([evidence](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/651)). Compatibility, satisfaction, and simulator traits remain unobserved; no improvement is claimed.

idea.description: Add an independently encoded five-interaction pathway to per-dataset SASRec, mix its features with full-history features through a learned scalar gate, and train with 128 uniform negatives using the exact published gBCE objective. Evaluate the components separately before selecting the combination.
idea.motivation: Recent-context gating addresses older or isolated interactions treated as current demand and broad historical associations displacing recent specific interests. Multiple-negative training addresses weak positive–negative separation, especially Electronics' 14.95% sampled wrong-ranking rate and negative lower-decile margin. These mechanisms cannot establish equipment compatibility, exhausted demand, ownership satisfaction, or user dislikes. Independent component ablations are essential because the supplied diagnostics do not establish which mechanism will improve macro validation HR@10.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four category routes, existing splits and pinned evaluator. Write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Preserve baseline architecture dimensions, optimizer, batch size and other hyperparameters unless explicitly listed as a variant. Use int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200')) as the epoch ceiling, subject to the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget; run all training single-GPU.

Architecture: share item embeddings, transformer blocks, normalization, positional embedding table and candidate scoring weights. For each valid supervised position, independently gather the raw item-ID suffix containing at most five interactions, left-pad to five, and encode it without access to full-history hidden states. Both branches assign position IDs 0 through branch_length-1 to their padded input slots; recent windows always use slots 0 through 4 during training and inference. Full-history inputs preserve the baseline's fixed-length positional policy. Padding positions are masked. The recent branch uses the final window feature; the full branch uses the corresponding causal full-history feature. Set g = sigmoid(w^T concat(full, recent) + b), initialize w=0 and b=log(0.1/0.9), and mix features as (1-g)*full + g*recent. Shared linear dot-product scoring makes this equivalent to mixing candidate scores. Keep baseline dropout; avoid extra time features or text features in this first experiment. Recency here means interaction order, not elapsed time.

Correct masking: apply causal and padding masks in both encoders. PyTorch MultiheadAttention boolean True blocks attention. Prevent fully masked padded query rows with a harmless fallback key, then clear their outputs; also clear padded states after blocks. Chunk independently encoded windows to control memory, preserving one mean over all valid supervised positions. In evaluation mode, verify that changing interactions before the final five leaves recent-branch features and scores unchanged. Verify padded, short-history, and train-versus-predictor score consistency. A sliding window in every layer has receptive field 1+D*(w-1), so it is not a substitute for independent five-token windows.

Loss and sampler: let N be the category's number of real items, excluding padding, and K=128. Require N>1. Use alpha=K/(N-1), beta=1-t+t*alpha, t=0.75. Draw negatives independently with replacement uniformly from all real item IDs, matching the official sampler, including possible target or known-positive collisions; never sample padding. This explicitly replaces the earlier proposed history exclusions. Excluding known training positives can be a separately labeled heuristic variant, but it invalidates direct transfer of the published calibration guarantee, and changing the denominator alone does not repair zero-probability exclusions. In float32 compute loss = mean_valid((beta*softplus(-positive_logit) + sum_j softplus(negative_logit_j))/(K+1)). Beta multiplies positive log-loss; do not use inverse-beta pos_weight, independently averaged positive/negative terms, or unstable sigmoid-power transformations. t=0 gives ordinary BCE with the same K-negative reduction, not equivalence to single-negative training. The sampler's possible false negatives are a limitation, not evidence that unobserved items are dislikes.

Efficiency: avoid unnecessarily materializing B*L*K*D negative embeddings at once; chunk supervised positions or candidate scoring and preserve exact loss normalization. Profile actual step time and peak GPU memory; count profiling, diagnostics, debugging, failed runs and all four-category trials against the shared budget. Published 128-negative convergence times were about 1.81x on Steam and 1.32x on Gowalla, not transferable per-epoch or memory multipliers. Independent recent-window encoding adds further cost.

Selection: predeclare four variants—baseline, gBCE-only, gate-only, combined—with checkpoint evaluation every 10 epochs, patience of five evaluations after the first evaluation, epoch ceiling 200 unless SASREC_EPOCHS overrides it, and earliest-checkpoint tie-breaking. Use one consistent checkpoint-selection rule based solely on unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10. Maintain an aggregate GPU-time ledger and reserve 10% of the total budget for diagnostics and final artifact checks; allocate the remaining time equally across variants and within each variant across categories. Budget exhaustion ends a run at its last completed checkpoint; record incomplete schedules and do not interpret them as matched convergence comparisons. Preserve category-level results and count all evaluated checkpoints as selection opportunities. If the unchanged evaluator exposes paired per-user validation hits, bootstrap users within each category with identical indices across models, average the four category differences, and report a 95% interval, category differences and discordant hits. One changed user hit is 0.5 percentage points within its category and 0.125 points in macro HR@10. These intervals condition on trained models and fixed candidate sets. Use Holm adjustment for planned variant-versus-baseline comparisons, while labeling post-selection inference exploratory; it does not remove adaptive selection optimism. Do not modify the evaluator to obtain unavailable outputs. Freeze selection before held-out evaluation.

Diagnostics and serving: preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics and definitions. view.model must remain the actual trained nn.Module. Expose mixed features through log2feats(sequence) and matching predict_score(features, items), retain item_emb, user_train, meta_data and review_data compatibility, and use view.model for architecture-dependent probes. Measure margins using actual mixed logits; mark unavailable category breakdowns unavailable rather than inventing metadata. Titles, descriptions, public histories and timestamps are the only permitted auxiliary information; review ratings/text, prices, stores and item categories are unavailable despite the generic input examples. Keep full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for the twenty diagnostic training users, five per category. Save gate parameters, window length, positional policy, model configuration, loss/sampler configuration and category routing with checkpoints. Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs the same shared encoder and independent final-window branch.

Shortcut risks: the gate can collapse to one branch or encode history-length shortcuts, while uniform-negative training can reward item popularity. Track gate distributions by history length, recent-versus-full disagreement, and observed training-popularity strata alongside existing diagnostics. These are exploratory measurements, not new selection metrics or evidence of user satisfaction. Keep the selected architecture small and avoid fitting thresholds to the twenty simulator users.
idea.pseudocode:
K = 128
for variant in [baseline, gBCE_only, gate_only, combined]:
    for category in FOUR_DATASETS:
        reset_training_seed(42)
        model = build_baseline_or_shared_window_model(variant)
        N = number_of_real_items(category)
        beta = 0.25 + 0.75 * K / (N - 1)
        for epoch in predeclared_epoch_and_GPU_budget:
            for _, sequence, positive, baseline_negative in train_loader:
                valid = positive != 0
                full = model.encode_full(sequence, causal=True)
                if variant_has_gate:
                    windows = gather_raw_left_padded_suffixes(sequence, valid, width=5)
                    recent = encode_independently_in_chunks(windows, positions=range(5))[:, -1]
                    h = full[valid]
                    g = sigmoid(model.gate(concat(h, recent)))
                    features = (1-g)*h + g*recent
                else:
                    features = full[valid]
                p = model.predict_score(features, positive[valid]).float()
                if variant_has_gBCE:
                    negatives = uniform_with_replacement(real_item_ids, shape=(valid.sum(), K))
                    n = model.predict_score(features, negatives).float()
                    loss = ((beta*softplus(-p) + softplus(n).sum(-1))/(K+1)).mean()
                else:
                    loss = unchanged_baseline_BCE(features, positive[valid], baseline_negative[valid])
                update_once(loss)
            every_10_epochs_evaluate_unchanged_validation_protocol()
            save_if_macro_HR10_improves_else_increment_patience()
            stop_if_patience_or_epoch_or_GPU_limit_reached()
        save_checkpoint_configuration_and_matching_predictor_writer()
select_variant_by_macro_validation_HR10_with_predeclared_ties()
run_measured_diagnostics_and_predictor_consistency_checks_within_reserved_budget()
freeze_selection_without_accessing_test_labels()

originality.positive: Combines independently controlled recent context and calibrated candidate competition in a compact, falsifiable adaptation.
originality.negative: Both mechanisms have established precedents; this is an incremental combination rather than a new model class.

future_potential.positive: Provides a practical framework for investigating interactions between temporal context selection and ranking supervision, with independent ablations.
future_potential.negative: Promise remains hypothetical: sparse histories, stable preferences, popularity shortcuts or compute costs may eliminate its advantage.

code_difficulty.positive: Shares SASRec parameters, retains dot-product scoring and existing category routing, and uses a short stable loss expression.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact independent-window encoding, padding safety, loss normalization, compute budgeting and matching predictor serialization make implementation harder than the original score of five suggested.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Uses multiple uniform negatives and calibrated gBCE to address sampled-BCE overconfidence.
Defines alpha=K/(N-1) and beta=1-t+t*alpha; beta weights positive log-loss within a joint K+1 candidate reduction.
limitations: Additional negatives increase compute; reported convergence-time ratios are dataset-specific and provide no matched peak-memory ratio.
Calibration claims depend on sampling assumptions and do not transfer unchanged to history-excluding samplers.
No supplied evidence establishes gains under the four-category pinned protocol.

related_work.title: Official gSASRec PyTorch training implementation
contributions: Provides the reference training reduction and positive-logit transformation, motivating an algebraically equivalent stable softplus implementation.
limitations: Clipping in the transformed-logit implementation can introduce numerical approximations.
Changing the relative positive/negative reduction creates a different objective.

related_work.title: Official gSASRec sampler
contributions: Samples real-item negatives uniformly with replacement without rejecting targets or known positives.
limitations: Allows target collisions and false negatives.
History-excluding sampling requires explicitly different assumptions.

related_work.title: HeteroTempRec
contributions: Combines local pattern extraction, global dependencies and personalized temporal fusion.
limitations: Motivates temporal fusion but does not validate the simplified shared-window adaptation.
Temporal relevance does not establish satisfied demand or equipment compatibility.

related_work.title: DTR4Rec
contributions: Fuses directed long-window transitions and short-window co-occurrences with sequence predictions.
limitations: Reported Amazon categories differ from the target benchmark.
Observed transitions do not identify complementarity or substitution.

related_work.title: Longformer
contributions: Provides a precedent for layered local attention and its expanding receptive field.
limitations: Stacked local attention does not enforce a fixed five-interaction information boundary.
Its language-model results do not establish recommendation gains.

related_work.title: PyTorch MultiheadAttention documentation
contributions: Documents attention and key-padding mask semantics needed for reproducible causal encoders.
limitations: Masking keys does not automatically clear padded query outputs.
Fully masked query rows require explicit handling.

related_work.title: Paired retrieval-evaluation research
contributions: Supports paired bootstrap or randomization approaches for retrieval comparisons.
limitations: Fixed-model, fixed-candidate bootstrap intervals exclude training-seed and candidate-sampling variability.
Post-selection intervals require exploratory interpretation.

related_work.title: On the Bias of Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can reverse model rankings.
limitations: Does not replace the mandated benchmark metric or justify changing its evaluator.
Sampled HR@10 gains alone cannot establish full-catalog ranking superiority.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains optimism introduced by repeated model selection on finite validation data.
limitations: Multiplicity adjustment alone does not remove adaptive checkpoint and variant selection bias.
Predeclared schedules reduce flexibility but cannot eliminate validation overfitting.
